name: Yo La Tengo
label: Matador
lede: A rock critic and a drummer from Hoboken went through roughly fifteen bass players before finding the one who stayed, then spent three decades making records that whisper, roar, and play eight nights of Hanukkah.

eras.title: A yellow tango in Hoboken
eras.text: Ira Kaplan and Georgia Hubley, a couple in Hoboken, New Jersey, started a band out of shared records: The Soft Boys, Mission of Burma, Love. The early line-ups changed almost every season, but the core never did.

years.h: Ira Kaplan and Georgia Hubley start Yo La Tengo in Hoboken
years.p: Ira Kaplan, a rock critic, and drummer Georgia Hubley, daughter of Oscar-winning animators John and Faith Hubley, form the band around their record collection. [[Dave Rick|6a5eae3e-3ee8-44bc-90d4-33bcc59f5c74]] plays bass.

years.big: What the hell is a yellow tango?
years.h: Yo La Tengo is named for a 1962 New York Mets collision
years.p: Mets outfielder Richie Ashburn learned to shout the Spanish phrase at shortstop Elio Chacón. Frank Thomas, who missed the meeting, ran into Ashburn anyway.
years.xp:
The story goes that Ashburn and Chacón kept colliding on fly balls, so Ashburn learned to yell the Spanish for I've got it. In the next game, left fielder Frank Thomas, who didn't speak Spanish, crashed into Ashburn and asked what a yellow tango was.

Wikipedia flags the provenance as shaky: Thomas is said to have claimed Ashburn made the whole thing up.

years.h: Debut single The River of Water, on Coyote Records
years.p: Yo La Tengo's first 7-inch pairs The River of Water with a cover of [[Arthur Lee|4e0a7e0d-bd05-4210-a654-72c4d437fda5]]'s A House Is Not a Motel. [[Dave Schramm|b06d3876-1fc4-4017-8cf9-da964b8a733a]] plays lead guitar.

years.h: Ride the Tiger, produced by Mission of Burma's Clint Conley
years.p: [[Clint Conley|a09560c0-4264-4341-af25-5727ca13417b]] of [[Mission of Burma|db9d25d7-a85b-4a29-b2ff-8f5b69ed691e]] produces the Coyote Records debut and plays bass on three songs. The sleeve credits Ira Kaplan with naive guitar.

years.h: Dave Schramm and Mike Lewis leave; Ira Kaplan takes lead guitar
years.p: After Ride the Tiger, guitarist Dave Schramm and bassist Mike Lewis both quit. Ira Kaplan moves to lead guitar and [[Stephan Wichnewski|9ea87f74-92cb-4ba2-9e26-f01d39a29212]] joins on bass.

eras.title: The bass player carousel
eras.text: With Kaplan now the guitarist, Yo La Tengo made its name with critics while cycling through bass players and even playing as a duo. Fakebook showed the quiet side that would matter as much as the noise.

years.h: New Wave Hot Dogs sells poorly but pushes forward
years.p: Yo La Tengo's second Coyote album moves beyond jangle into more guitar noise. It sells poorly.

years.h: President Yo La Tengo wins over the critics
years.p: Produced by [[Gene Holder|f35abb6b-cd8a-4f61-98c3-880e0d4a98dd]] of [[The dB's|d2a54937-fd0d-4586-85c3-235a405019cf]], the last Coyote album makes Yo La Tengo's reputation. Robert Christgau praised the guitar hook of opener Barnaby, Hardly Working.

years.h: Stephan Wichnewski leaves; Yo La Tengo plays as a duo
years.p: With bassist Stephan Wichnewski gone, Ira Kaplan and Georgia Hubley play shows as a two-piece with two electric guitars.

years.h: Fakebook: acoustic covers of Cat Stevens, the Kinks, Daniel Johnston
years.p: Dave Schramm returns for a mostly acoustic Bar/None album of covers by [[Cat Stevens|e2345fdf-2be7-47c5-a6dd-be64353ad134]], [[Gene Clark|2b6f3780-6fb6-42c2-95bb-5e080772e38c]], [[The Kinks|17b53d9f-5c63-4a09-a593-dde4608e0db9]] and [[Daniel Johnston|8a7ca8b0-d23c-4eff-8fe9-6220ba5c9c76]], plus a quiet redo of Barnaby, Hardly Working.

years.h: Yo La Tengo backs Daniel Johnston on Speeding Motorcycle
years.p: Yo La Tengo collaborates with [[Daniel Johnston|8a7ca8b0-d23c-4eff-8fe9-6220ba5c9c76]] on the single Speeding Motorcycle. The same year brings the That Is Yo La Tengo EP and a Beat Happening cover, Cast a Shadow.

years.h: James McNew joins as a fill-in bassist and never leaves
years.p: [[James McNew|4182b4da-dc89-4331-bca0-952369bb63fb]] signs on only for a US tour and a four-week European run with [[Eleventh Dream Day|751b1385-9595-46ee-b634-8f90f892682a]]. He becomes the fifteenth-odd bass player and the last.
years.xp:
The European leg had its mishaps: after a show in Münster, McNew left a box of merchandise behind at the club, and only realized it at soundcheck in Hamburg the next day.

By 1992 Kaplan, Hubley and McNew were a fixed trio, the line-up that has lasted ever since. McNew also records on his own as [[Dump|2d9215eb-0d46-4624-b155-2a0f32482a4e]].

eras.title: Three people, one sound
eras.text: With James McNew locked in and producer Roger Moutenot on board, Yo La Tengo signed to Matador Records and found the balance of feedback and hush that defines it. By 1997 critics were calling a Yo La Tengo album a masterpiece.

years.h: May I Sing with Me, recorded in Boston for Alias
years.p: Gene Holder produces and Lou Giordano engineers. Three songs carry over from the That Is Yo La Tengo EP with Holder on bass.

years.h: Yo La Tengo signs to Matador and releases Shaker
years.p: The partnership with Matador Records begins with the single Shaker, recorded with John Siket in New Jersey. It has lasted more than thirty years.

q: I think this group really started when we made the record Painful
years.src: Wikipedia · The New Rolling Stone Album Guide
years.h: Painful, the record where the trio begins
years.p: The first Yo La Tengo album with James McNew on every song and the first produced by Roger Moutenot. Rob Sheffield said it kept every promise the band ever made.
years.xp:
Painful opens and closes with two versions of Big Day Coming, one a slow drone, one a buzzing rocker. From a Motel 6 became an early Matador favorite.

Stephen Thomas Erlewine called the album subtly addicting. The long run with Moutenot as producer lasted until 2013.

years.h: Electr-O-Pura: every song now credited to the band
years.p: For the first time every song is credited to Yo La Tengo as a whole rather than to individuals, and it stays that way.

years.h: Yo La Tengo plays the Velvet Underground in I Shot Andy Warhol
years.p: Critics had compared them to [[The Velvet Underground|94b0fb9d-a066-4823-b2ec-af1d324bcfcf]] for years. In Mary Harron's 1996 film, Yo La Tengo appears as an anonymous version of the band.

years.h: I Can Hear the Heart Beating as One gets a 9.7 from Pitchfork
years.p: Folk, punk, shoegaze drones, bossa nova and noise jams on one Matador album. AllMusic called it arguably the band's finest and most coherent record.
years.xp: Kaplan said that after Electr-O-Pura the band stopped worrying about what the next record should sound like. The result runs from the drone of Spec Bebop to the Beach Boys-style Sugarcube to Stockholm Syndrome, sung by James McNew.
play: I Can Hear the Heart Beating as One

years.h: Mr. Show's Bob Odenkirk and David Cross star in the Sugarcube video
years.p: The video for Sugarcube, from I Can Hear the Heart Beating as One, sends Yo La Tengo to rock school run by Bob Odenkirk and David Cross of Mr. Show.

eras.title: Loud, quiet, and eight nights of Hanukkah
eras.text: Yo La Tengo spent the next decade doing everything at once: whisper-quiet albums, film scores, a collaboration with Yoko Ono, radio marathons and a holiday residency that became a Hoboken tradition.

years.h: Salvation Army band in Hal Hartley's The Book of Life
years.p: Yo La Tengo appears as a Salvation Army band in Hal Hartley's film and makes Strange but True with [[Jad Fair|be4a8e65-a7ba-474c-989b-ed16e51c1a39]] of [[Half Japanese|18dc6bd7-9caa-4c2d-a2fc-e9546ebda6a4]].

years.h: And Then Nothing Turned Itself Inside-Out closes on 17 minutes
years.p: The hushed album ends with Night Falls on Hoboken, a 17-minute meditation on the band's home town.
play: And Then Nothing Turned Itself Inside-Out

years.h: The Sounds of the Sounds of Science debuts in San Francisco
years.p: Yo La Tengo scores eight undersea documentaries by French filmmaker Jean Painlevé for the San Francisco Film Festival, then performs it live about a dozen times.

years.h: Eight nights of Hanukkah at Maxwell's begin
years.p: Yo La Tengo starts playing all eight nights of Hanukkah at Maxwell's in Hoboken, with surprise guests and comedians and proceeds going to charity. It becomes an annual pilgrimage.

years.h: Summer Sun leaves the loud songs off
years.p: Ira Kaplan said the band decided at the last second to drop the loud songs. Some critics found the quiet album underwhelming. The same year, they record with [[Yoko Ono|b0b33754-a664-43b7-ba00-be0dc4ec2396]] for a Harvey Milk High School benefit.

years.h: I Am Not Afraid of You and I Will Beat Your Ass
years.p: Yo La Tengo's eleventh album opens and closes with guitar jams over ten minutes each, with strings and horns in between. It lands to near-universal acclaim.
play: I Am Not Afraid of You and I Will Beat Your Ass
Pass the Hatchet, I Think I'm Goodkind

years.h: Murdering the Classics: covers requested by WFMU pledge callers
years.p: For years Yo La Tengo played New Jersey radio station WFMU's pledge drive, attempting any song a caller requested on the spot. Yo La Tengo Is Murdering the Classics collects the wreckage.

years.h: The Freewheelin' Yo La Tengo takes questions from the crowd
years.p: An acoustic tour where the audience requests songs and asks the band questions between them.

years.h: Yo La Tengo plays as the Condo Fucks in Brooklyn
years.p: The trio plays Brooklyn's Magnetic Field under the name Condo Fucks. In March 2009 Matador releases the alias's garage covers album, Fuckbook.

years.h: Popular Songs enters the Billboard 200 at No. 58
years.p: Recorded in the band's New Jersey rehearsal space, with string arrangements by jazz composer Richard Evans on two songs. No. 58 was Yo La Tengo's highest chart entry to that point.

eras.title: Still the same three
eras.text: Maxwell's closed, the Hanukkah shows moved on, and Yo La Tengo kept releasing records on Matador, from a pandemic album recorded on one microphone to a return to noise in 2023.

years.h: Jesse Jarnow's book Big Day Coming tells the band's story
years.p: Jesse Jarnow's history of Yo La Tengo, named after the Painful song, traces the band and the rise of indie rock around it.

years.h: Fade: the first album produced by John McEntire
years.p: [[John McEntire|73e452bb-1f86-4dec-a2aa-a8b097fea4c6]] of [[Tortoise|e0953daa-860f-4dc8-9f1a-b12587cdaf17]] produces, ending Roger Moutenot's run since Painful.

years.h: Maxwell's, where the Hanukkah shows began, closes
years.p: The Hoboken club that hosted Yo La Tengo's holiday run shuts its doors in 2013. The Hanukkah shows later continue in Manhattan.

years.h: Yo La Tengo plays Bobby Night Ranger on Parks and Recreation
years.p: In the season 6 finale, the band appears as a Night Ranger cover band. It also tours The Love Song of R. Buckminster Fuller with filmmaker Sam Green narrating live.

years.h: Stuff Like That There: Dave Schramm returns for a Fakebook sequel
years.p: Dave Schramm rejoins for re-recorded old songs and covers of [[The Cure|69ee3720-a7cb-4402-b48d-a02c366f2bcf]], [[Hank Williams|906bddec-bc73-49f8-ac1e-eaee691c6cf9]] and [[Sun Ra|c27cac8e-4c4a-48c0-a4ba-41399b9c176d]].

years.h: There's a Riot Going On borrows a Sly Stone title
years.p: Pitchfork said Yo La Tengo's fifteenth album reflects the group's greatest and most recognizable strengths.

years.h: We Have Amnesia Sometimes: recorded on one microphone
years.p: Over ten days in late April and early May 2020, the trio records five ambient instrumentals, socially distanced under New Jersey's pandemic rules.

years.h: This Stupid World, album seventeen
years.p: Yo La Tengo's seventeenth studio album, on Matador, nearly four decades after the first single.
